picture.summary: A simple one-page site with a dark top menu, a warm coral banner with a big centered title, a row of three matching cards on a cream background, and a dark footer.

sections.name: a top menu
sections.description: A dark brown bar with the bold white site name 'My Site' on the left and four white links (Home, About, Work, Contact) on the right.

sections.name: a big banner
sections.description: A wide coral-orange block with a large bold white title 'Big Title Here' centered and a smaller white line of text beneath it.

sections.name: 3 cards
sections.description: Three white cards with rounded corners and a thin gray border sitting side by side on a cream background, each with a peach picture placeholder, a bold dark title, and two gray bars standing in for text.

sections.name: a footer
sections.description: A dark brown bar at the bottom with centered white text reading 'Footer · made by me'.

title: A warm one-page site with cards
summary: You will build a friendly one-page website with a dark top menu, a coral banner with a big title, three matching cards on a cream background and a dark footer. A few lines of JavaScript let visitors pick a favourite card.
outcome: A finished, offline website (index.html, style.css and script.js) that looks like your picture and highlights a card when you click it.

simpler.title: Just a banner and one card
simpler.why: You'll build a real styled page with a warm banner and a card in well under an hour, and you can add the menu, more cards and the click fun later.

steps.title: Start the page
steps.instruction: In index.html, type the basic page frame: the doctype line, the html tag, and a head with the character set, the screen-size line, a title saying My Site and a link to style.css. Close the head and the html.
steps.why: Every web page needs this frame so the browser knows what it is reading.
steps.expected:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>My Site</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
</html>

checks.say: I can't see your page title yet.
Your page isn't linked to the style file yet.
checks.name: href

checks.say: The line that fits the page to phone screens is missing.
checks.name: content

checks.say: Something in the page frame looks broken.

hints: A page starts with a line saying it is HTML, then an html tag holding a head section.
Inside <head> you need <meta charset>, <meta name="viewport">, <title> and <link rel="stylesheet">.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  …
  <title>…</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="…">
</head>
</html>

concept.title: Tags
concept.explain: HTML uses tags in angle brackets, like <title>, and most come in pairs that open and close around something.
concept.imageQuery: html page structure diagram head body
concept.videoQuery: html basic page structure for beginners

steps.title: Add the top bar
steps.instruction: Under the closing head tag, add a body. Inside it, add a header with the class menu and id home, holding a link with the class logo that says My Site and goes to #home.
steps.why: The body holds everything visitors see, starting with your top bar.
steps.expected: My Site

checks.say: I can't see your top bar yet.
Your logo link should say My Site.
Your logo link should jump to the top of the page.
checks.name: href

hints: Everything you can see goes inside a body, and the top bar is a header.
After </head>, write <body>, then a <header class="menu" id="home"> with an <a class="logo"> inside.
…

concept.title: Classes and ids
concept.explain: A class is a name tag we can style later; an id is a unique name a link can jump to.

steps.title: Add the menu links
steps.instruction: Inside the header, under the logo link, add a nav with four links: Home to #home, About to #about, Work to #work and Contact to #contact.
steps.why: These links let visitors jump to each part of your page.
steps.expected: Home About Work Contact

checks.say: I can't see your four menu links yet.
Your Contact link should go to #contact.
checks.name: href

checks.say: One of your menu links should say About.

hints: A group of menu links lives in its own little box inside the header.
Under the logo link, add <nav> and put four <a href="#…"> links inside it.
Home … …

concept.title: Links
concept.explain: An a tag makes a link; its href says where clicking it takes you, and # means a spot on this page.

steps.title: Add the banner
steps.instruction: Under the header, add a section with the class banner and id about. Inside it, put a big heading saying Big Title Here and a short line of friendly text.
steps.why: The banner is the first big message visitors read.
steps.expected:
Big Title Here

A small line of friendly text about my site.

checks.say: I can't see your banner yet.
Your banner needs a big heading.
Your banner needs a short line of text under the heading.

hints: Make a new part of the page for a big title and a sentence.

concept.title: Headings and paragraphs
concept.explain: h1 is the biggest heading on a page, and p holds a normal paragraph of text.

steps.title: Add the first card
steps.instruction: Under the banner, add a main with the class cards and id work. Inside it, add an article with the class card holding a div with the class picture and a 🌻, a smaller heading First Card, and a short note.
steps.why: Cards are neat boxes that show one thing each.
steps.expected:
🌻

First Card

A short note about this first thing.

checks.say: I can't see your first card yet.
Your card needs a picture box.
Your card needs a heading.

hints: You need a box for all the cards, and the first card inside it.
After the banner's </section>, add <main class="cards" id="work"> with an <article class="card"> inside.

🌻

concept.title: Boxes inside boxes
concept.explain: Tags can sit inside other tags, like a card inside a group of cards, building the page from boxes.

steps.title: Add two more cards
steps.instruction: Inside the cards box, under the first card, add two more cards the same way: one with 🎨 and Second Card, one with 📚 and Third Card.
steps.why: Three matching cards make the page look full and tidy.
steps.expected:
🎨

Second Card

A short note about this second thing.

📚

Third Card

A short note about this third thing.

checks.say: I can only see one card so far; you need three.
Every card needs its own picture box.

hints: Copy the shape of your first card twice and change the words.
Under the first </article>, add two more <article class="card"> blocks, each with a picture, h2 and p.

🎨

Second Card

steps.title: Add the footer and script
steps.instruction: Under the cards box, add a footer with the class footer and id contact holding a line saying Footer · made by me. Below it, add a script tag that loads script.js.
steps.why: The footer closes the page, and the script tag gets it ready for clicks later.
steps.expected: Footer · made by me

checks.say: I can't see your footer yet.
Your footer should say who made the page.
Your page isn't loading script.js yet.

steps.title: Look at your page
steps.instruction: Open index.html in the browser. All your words are there, but it's plain black and white for now.
steps.why: Seeing the plain page shows how much the styling will change.
hints: Just open the page in your browser and look.
Find index.html and open it in the browser.
Scroll down: menu, banner, three cards, footer.

quiz.question: Which tag holds everything visitors see on the page?
quiz.explain: The body holds all the visible content; the head holds information about the page.

steps.title: Set the page colours
steps.instruction: In style.css, add a rule for everything that sets box-sizing to border-box, then a body rule with no margin, the Arial font, a cream background #f9f6f1 and dark text #3c3031.
steps.why: This gives the whole page its warm cream look and a clean font.

checks.say: Your page background isn't cream yet.
The page still has a gap around its edges.
Boxes should count their padding inside their size.
Something in your style file looks broken.

hints: Write one rule for every box, then one for the body.
Use * { box-sizing: … } and body { margin, font-family, background, color }.

concept.title: CSS rules
concept.explain: A CSS rule names what to style, then lists changes inside curly brackets, each like property: value;.

steps.title: Make the menu a dark bar
steps.instruction: Below the body rule, add a .menu rule that lines things up in a row with flex, pushes them to each end, centres them up and down, adds padding 16px 32px and a dark background #3c3031.
steps.why: Your logo and links now sit side by side on a dark bar.

checks.say: Your menu items aren't side by side yet.
Your logo and links should be pushed to opposite ends.
Your menu bar isn't dark yet.

hints: Make the menu line its contents up in a row and give it a dark colour.
Add .menu { … } with display: flex, justify-content, align-items, padding and background.

concept.title: Flexbox
concept.explain: display: flex puts the things inside a box in a row and lets you space them out easily.

steps.title: White menu text and a bold logo
steps.instruction: Add a rule for links in the menu that makes them white with no underline, then a .logo rule with size 22px and bold text.
steps.why: White text stands out on the dark bar, and the logo looks like a logo.

checks.say: Your menu links aren't white yet.
Your logo should be bigger.
Your logo should be bold.

hints: Style the links inside the menu, then the logo on its own.
Write .menu a { color, text-decoration } and .logo { font-size, font-weight }.

steps.title: Space the links and add hover
steps.instruction: Add a nav a rule with a left margin of 20px, then a nav a:hover rule that turns the link peach #f2c6a5.
steps.why: Links get room to breathe and light up when the mouse is over them.

checks.say: Your menu links still sit too close together.
Your links don't change colour when the mouse is over them yet.
checks.question: Does style.css have a nav a:hover rule that changes the link colour?

hints: Give each link some space on its left, then a colour for when the mouse touches it.
Use nav a { margin-left } and nav a:hover { color }.

concept.title: Hover
concept.explain: Adding :hover to a rule makes its style apply only while the mouse is on top of it.

steps.title: Colour the banner
steps.instruction: Add a .banner rule with padding 80px 20px, a coral background #e07b60, white text and centred text.
steps.why: The banner becomes a big, warm coral block that grabs attention.

checks.say: Your banner isn't coral yet.
Your banner text should be in the middle.
Your banner needs more space inside it.

hints: Give the banner space, a coral colour and centred white words.
Write .banner { padding, background, color, text-align }.

concept.title: Padding
concept.explain: Padding is the empty space inside a box, between its edge and what's inside.

steps.title: Size the banner words
steps.instruction: Add a .banner h1 rule with margin 0 0 12px and size 48px, then a .banner p rule with no margin and size 18px.
steps.why: The title becomes big and bold while the line under it stays gentle.

checks.say: Your big title isn't big enough yet.
The line under your title should be a little bigger.

hints: Style the heading inside the banner, then the paragraph inside it.
Write .banner h1 { margin, font-size } and .banner p { margin, font-size }.

quiz.question: What does nav a:hover change?
options: How links look all the time
How links look while the mouse is over them
quiz.explain: :hover only applies while the mouse is on the link.

steps.title: Line up the cards
steps.instruction: Add a .cards rule that uses flex, lets cards wrap to a new line, centres them, puts a 24px gap between them and adds padding 48px 20px.
steps.why: Your three cards now sit side by side and wrap nicely on small screens.

checks.say: Your cards aren't side by side yet.
Your cards should be able to move to a new line.
Your cards need some space between them.

hints: Use the same row trick as the menu, but let the cards wrap and keep a gap.
Write .cards { display: flex; flex-wrap; justify-content; gap; padding }.

concept.title: Gap and wrap
concept.explain: gap puts equal space between items in a row, and flex-wrap lets them move to a new line when there's no room.

steps.title: Shape each card
steps.instruction: Add a .card rule with width 260px, padding 16px, a white background, a thin border 1px solid #dad5ce, rounded corners of 12px and a pointer cursor.
steps.why: Each card becomes a white rounded box that looks clickable.

checks.say: Your cards aren't the right width yet.
Your cards need rounded corners.
The mouse should turn into a pointing hand over a card.

hints: Give each card a size, white colour, a thin edge and soft corners.
Write .card { width, padding, background, border, border-radius, cursor }.

concept.title: Borders and round corners
concept.explain: border draws a line around a box, and border-radius rounds its corners.

steps.title: Style the picture box
steps.instruction: Add a .picture rule: height 140px, corners 8px, a peach background #f2c6a5, flex with the emoji centred both ways, and size 56px.
steps.why: Each emoji sits big and centred in a soft peach box.

checks.say: Your picture boxes aren't peach yet.
Your picture boxes should be taller.
The emoji should be centred in its box.

hints: Make a tall peach box and put the emoji right in the middle.
Write .picture { height, border-radius, background, display: flex, justify-content, align-items, font-size }.

steps.title: Style the card words
steps.instruction: Add a .card h2 rule with margin 16px 0 8px and size 20px, then a .card p rule with no margin and a soft grey colour #8a817c.
steps.why: The card titles stand out and the notes look calm and readable.

checks.say: Your card titles aren't the right size yet.
Your card notes should be soft grey.

hints: Style the heading in a card, then the paragraph in a card.
Write .card h2 { margin, font-size } and .card p { margin, color }.

steps.title: Style the footer
steps.instruction: At the end of the file, add a .footer rule with padding 20px, a dark background #3c3031, white text and centred text.
steps.why: A dark footer matches the menu and neatly closes the page.

checks.say: Your footer isn't dark yet.
Your footer text should be white.
Your footer text should be centred.

hints: It looks a lot like the banner rule, just darker.
Write .footer { padding, background, color, text-align }.

steps.title: Admire your styled page
steps.instruction: Refresh the browser. You should see a dark menu, a coral banner, three white cards on cream and a dark footer.
steps.why: You can see how CSS turned plain text into a real website.
hints: Refresh the page in your browser.
Press the refresh button or Ctrl+R.
Try making the window narrow and watch the cards wrap.

quiz.question: Which line lets the cards move to a new row on a small screen?
quiz.explain: flex-wrap: wrap lets items move onto a new line when there's no room.

steps.title: Get a highlight ready
steps.instruction: In style.css, under the .card rule, add a .card.picked rule with a thicker coral border: 3px solid #e07b60.
steps.why: This is the look a card will get once a visitor picks it.

checks.say: I can't see the coral highlight for a picked card yet.
checks.question: Does style.css have a .card.picked rule that sets a 3px solid coral (#e07b60) border?

checks.say: Something in your style file looks broken.

hints: Write a style for a card that also has the name picked.
Use .card.picked with no space, and set a border.

concept.title: Two class names together
concept.explain: Writing .card.picked styles only cards that also carry the extra name picked.

steps.title: Pick a card on click
steps.instruction: In script.js, find all the cards and save them as cards. Then for each card, listen for a click and add the picked name to that card.
steps.why: Clicking a card now gives it the coral highlight.

checks.say: Clicking a card doesn't highlight it yet.
checks.question: Does script.js select all .card elements and add a click listener to each one that adds the class "picked"?

checks.say: I can't find your script.js file.
Something in your code file looks broken.

hints: First grab every card, then go through them one by one and tell each to react to a click.
Use document.querySelectorAll(".card"), then cards.forEach, card.addEventListener("click", …) and classList.add.

concept.title: Listening for clicks
concept.explain: JavaScript can wait for a click on something and then run your instructions, like adding a highlight.

steps.title: Only one favourite
steps.instruction: Inside the click part, just above the line that adds picked, go through all the cards and remove picked from each one.
steps.why: Now only one card can be the favourite at a time.

checks.say: More than one card can still be picked at once.
checks.question: Inside the click handler, does script.js loop over all cards and remove the class "picked" before adding it to the clicked card?

checks.say: Something in your code file looks broken.

hints: Before highlighting the clicked card, clear the highlight from all the others.
Above card.classList.add, use cards.forEach with classList.remove("picked").

concept.title: Removing a class
concept.explain: classList.remove takes a name off something, so its special style goes away.

steps.title: Pick your favourite
steps.instruction: Refresh the browser and click different cards. Only the last one you clicked gets the coral border.
steps.why: You made your page react to visitors.
hints: Refresh and click a card.
Click one card, then another, and watch the border move.
If nothing happens, check the script tag at the bottom of index.html.

quiz.question: Why do we remove picked from every card before adding it?
options: So only the clicked card is highlighted
To make the page load faster
quiz.explain: Clearing all highlights first means just one card stays picked.
